children: Shares of Nvidia fell after-hours after the New York Times reported that Chief Executive Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with an executive at the company.
The stock slipped 3.9%, to $167.02, after Wednesday's closing bell, more than erasing the 2.9% gain from the regular trading session. Shares of Nvidia competitor AMD, however, rose 1.6%, to $562.22.
The Times reported that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, citing people familiar with the matter.
Nvidia declined to comment to the Times.

The report adds to a growing firestorm surrounding Huang, who had a separate relationship with a woman suspected of sharing information with the Chinese government. Independent directors on Nvidia's board are investigating whether Huang was the target of a foreign espionage effort.
